title: introduce-late-arrival-buffering-and-cutpoint-anchoring-for-sse
author: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: We continue to see a class of partial-JSON failures and out-of-order function-call events when SSE events are delayed or arrive in bursty network conditions (mobile and long-tail proxies). This PR introduces a late-arrival buffering mode and a cutpoint anchoring heuristic to make stream reassembly more deterministic while preserving low-latency delivery for common-case fast-paths.

Summary of changes: Adds an adaptive late-arrival buffer that temporarily holds extremely small tail chunks to allow cutpoint anchoring (a lightweight checkpoint on multi-chunk JSON spans) to complete before emitting partial JSON. The anchoring heuristic uses sequence hints from the OpenAI-compat adapter, stabilizes token/event ordering by associating toolcall handoff tokens with cutpoints, and ensures that UTF-8 split bytes are not emitted as separate JSON fragments. The change is opt-in behind a feature flag (SSE_LATE_ARRIVAL_BUFFER) and tuned to default off for very low-latency customers; default behavior is conservative (enables only when average chunk size < 24 bytes or when reassembly error rate exceeds a threshold).

Compatibility and guarantees: No breaking API changes. The feature improves eventual JSON reconstruction and deterministic function/toolcall ordering; it may introduce microsecond-level additional latency in pathological chunk streams. Backwards-compatible with existing OpenAI-compat consumers and streaming clients; adapter emits an anchor token in metadata comments for observability when the buffer is engaged.

Testing and rollout plan: Unit tests and deterministic fuzz cases added for UTF-8 split, delimiter-loss, and interleaved toolcall scenarios. Integrations added to openai_compat test harness and to the streaming e2e simulator. Canary rollout to 5% of streaming traffic with observability flags and auto-disable if error budget impacts are observed.

commits_summary:
- feat(sse): add late-arrival buffer and cutpoint anchoring logic (parser and runtime)
- fix(openai_compat): emit sequence hint metadata for anchors
- test(sse): add fuzzed reassembly cases and UTF-8 split regression tests
- docs: describe feature flag and rollout guidance
- perf: microbenchmarks and threshold tuning results
changed_files: sse/parser.rs (core reassembly & anchor logic), sse/window.rs (buffer window policy), openai_compat/adapter.py (sequence hints and anchor emission), streaming/tests/sse_reassembly_test.go (deterministic cases), streaming/e2e/simulator.py (burst network simulation), docs/streaming/anchors.md (operator guide), pkg/config/flags.go (SSE_LATE_ARRIVAL_BUFFER flag), ci/benchmarks/sse_microbench.md
small_snippets: parser.rs: added anchor point enum and comment explaining nonblocking flush semantics; adapter.py: added _emit_anchor_hint() with metadata comment format; sse_reassembly_test.go: added table-driven cases for multi-chunk utf8-split
review_conversation:
Priya: Looks good overall, can you justify the buffer thresholds? Please add a short note on rollback behavior if enabled by mistake.
Avery: Thresholds come from 95th percentile chunk histograms; added doc section and a config knob for quick rollback.
Marcel: Unit tests are great but I observed flaky e2e on arm builders. Can we gate the heavy fuzz tests on linux-amd64-only in CI?
Avery: Added selective CI tags and reduced parallel seed range on arm builders; reran CI.
Sofia: Suggest splitting the openai_compat change so non-compat users don't pay; also request a small benchmark showing median latency impact.
Avery: Kept compatibility emission behind a config flag and added median latency numbers to bench notes.
Approvals: Priya approved after docs update, Marcel approved after CI noise reduction, Sofia approved after split and bench numbers. Merge ready.
ci_checks: Initial CI: fail (flaky e2e on arm), rerun: pass. Checks: go-test (pass), rust-test (pass), python-test (pass), streaming-integration (pass, gated), benchmarks (pass). Coverage: +0.4% on sse package. Notes: e2e flake traced to dynamic seed on arm; fixed by gating.
release_notes:
- Improved SSE streaming resilience: late-arrival buffering and cutpoint anchoring to reduce partial-JSON emits and toolcall reordering.
- Config: SSE_LATE_ARRIVAL_BUFFER (off by default).
- Observability: anchor-hint metadata emitted when buffering engages.
notes_for_release_manager: Feature is behind SSE_LATE_ARRIVAL_BUFFER flag and opt-in for initial canary. Recommend enabling for hosted streaming canary only and monitoring sse.reassembly.errors and sse.anchor_engaged metrics. Rolling back is a single config flip. Inform customer success of change to help troubleshoot any low-latency complaints.
qa_notes: Run streaming/e2e/simulator.py with burst and probe modes, validate that function-call order matches expected sequence in streaming/tests/fixtures/toolcall_order.json. Check that no additional partial JSONs are emitted in the majority of runs; validate anchor-hint presence in 100% of buffered cases.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: behavioural change in rare network patterns. No schema or API break. Potential small latency increase under pathological chunking. Feature is gated and reversible.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-4187: telemetry dashboard for anchor engagement; ENG-4192: expose per-customer flag in console; ENG-4195: apply tuned thresholds to Dedicated clusters
notes: This PR addresses long-tail fragmentation issues observed in mobile and proxy-heavy customers and is crafted to be reversible and observable during canary. The approach prioritizes deterministic ordering for tool calls and safe UTF-8 handling while minimizing default impact.
